newsitem.title: USA: Electric body says EPA scapegoated industry.
newsitem.headline: Electric body says EPA scapegoated industry.

text.p: The Edison Electric Institute, which represents electric utilities delivering three quarters of U.S. power, said on Wednesday that proposed legislation to tighten emissions at power plants was mistaken.

"Over-controlling power plants will not really improve the air we all breathe because our plants are just one of the many players whose emissions form ozone and particulate pollution, a simple fact the EPA would know if they'd finish their science homework," said Thomas Kuhn, the institute's president.
The EPA earlier today proposed tighter controls on the power industry including setting a limit on particle and ozone emissions.
Edison Electric Institute said that the Council of Economic Advisors had costed the EPA's ozone proposals at $60 billion across cars, factories and utilities. ((-- New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
